From b4b64fda4d30a83a7f00e92a0c8a1d47699609f3 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Johan Hovold <johan@kernel.org>
Date: Thu, 18 Dec 2025 16:35:16 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] usb: phy: isp1301: fix non-OF device reference imbalance

A recent change fixing a device reference leak in a UDC driver
introduced a potential use-after-free in the non-OF case as the
isp1301_get_client() helper only increases the reference count for the
returned I2C device in the OF case.

Increment the reference count also for non-OF so that the caller can
decrement it unconditionally.

Note that this is inherently racy just as using the returned I2C device
is since nothing is preventing the PHY driver from being unbound while
in use.

Fixes: c84117912bdd ("USB: lpc32xx_udc: Fix error handling in probe")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Cc: Ma Ke <make24@iscas.ac.cn>
Signed-off-by: Johan Hovold <johan@kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: Vladimir Zapolskiy <vz@mleia.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20251218153519.19453-3-johan@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

diff --git a/drivers/usb/phy/phy-isp1301.c b/drivers/usb/phy/phy-isp1301.c
index f9b5c411aee4..2940f0c84e1b 100644
--- a/drivers/usb/phy/phy-isp1301.c
+++ b/drivers/usb/phy/phy-isp1301.c
@@ -149,7 +149,12 @@ struct i2c_client *isp1301_get_client(struct device_node *node)
 		return client;
 
 	/* non-DT: only one ISP1301 chip supported */
-	return isp1301_i2c_client;
+	if (isp1301_i2c_client) {
+		get_device(&isp1301_i2c_client->dev);
+		return isp1301_i2c_client;
+	}
+
+	return NULL;
 }
 EXPORT_SYMBOL_GPL(isp1301_get_client);
 
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary

The patch fixes a device reference imbalance in the `isp1301_get_client()` function for non-OF (Device Tree) systems.

### Modifications in `drivers/usb/phy/phy-isp1301.c`

- **Changed the non-OF return path** (lines 149–155): Instead of directly returning the global `isp1301_i2c_client` pointer without incrementing the device reference count, the new code conditionally gets a reference (`get_device()`) before returning, ensuring the caller can later decrement it unconditionally. If `isp1301_i2c_client` is `NULL`, it now returns `NULL` instead of simply returning `NULL` implicitly (the previous code would have returned `NULL` only if `isp1301_i2c_client` was `NULL`, but the reference was never incremented when it was non-`NULL`).

### Relationship between changes

The fix is localized to the non-OF code path inside `isp1301_get_client()`. Previously, only the OF path (via `of_find_i2c_device_by_node()`) incremented the reference count; the non-OF path returned the raw pointer without a reference. This inconsistency meant that callers (e.g., `lpc32xx_udc` driver after a recent fix) would unconditionally call `put_device()`, leading to a potential use-after-free because the reference count could drop to zero prematurely. The change makes both OF and non-OF paths return a properly referenced I2C device, aligning their behavior and fixing the imbalance.

Here is the commit message:
usb: phy: isp1301: fix non-OF device reference imbalance

A recent change fixing a device reference leak in a UDC driver
introduced a potential use-after-free in the non-OF case as the
isp1301_get_client() helper only increases the reference count for the
returned I2C device in the OF case.

Increment the reference count also for non-OF so that the caller can
decrement it unconditionally.

Note that this is inherently racy just as using the returned I2C device
is since nothing is preventing the PHY driver from being unbound while
in use.

Fixes: c84117912bdd ("USB: lpc32xx_udc: Fix error handling in probe")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Cc: Ma Ke <make24@iscas.ac.cn>
Signed-off-by: Johan Hovold <johan@kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: Vladimir Zapolskiy <vz@mleia.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20251218153519.19453-3-johan@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

Here is the root cause:
The function `isp1301_get_client()` in the ISP1301 PHY driver did not increment the device reference count (`get_device()`) when returning the I2C client in the non-OF (Device Tree) code path. This caused an unbalanced reference count when callers (such as the LPC32xx UDC driver after a fix that added unconditional `put_device()`) would decrement the reference, potentially dropping it to zero prematurely and leading to a use-after-free if the PHY driver was unbound.

Here is the patch:
 
 struct i2c_client *isp1301_get_client(struct device_node *node)
 {
 	struct i2c_client *client;
 
 	/* reference of ISP1301 I2C node via DT */
 	client = of_find_i2c_device_by_node(node);
 	if (client)
 		return client;
 
 	/* non-DT: only one ISP1301 chip supported */
-	return isp1301_i2c_client;
+	if (isp1301_i2c_client) {
+		get_device(&isp1301_i2c_client->dev);
+		return isp1301_i2c_client;
+	}
+
+	return NULL;
 }
 EXPORT_SYMBOL_GPL(isp1301_get_client);
